Author: Sujoy Paul
Bench: Sujoy Paul
In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Cra No. 1580 of 2023
(Shubham Chouhan @Kala Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others) Dated :
16-01-2024 Shri Siddharth Datt - Advocate for appellant.
Shri Ajay Shukla- Government Advocate for the State.
Heard on I.A. No.13650/2023, an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of
sentence and grant of bail to appellant Shubham Chouhan @ Kala arising out of judgment dated
23.12.2022 delivered in Special Case No. 194/2021 by XVIIIth Additional Sessions Judge/Special
Judge (Pocso Act) Bhopal.

entities.text: High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The appellant has been convicted under Section 5(L) read with Section 6 of Protection of Children
from Sexual Offence Act, read with Section 376(2)(n) of the Ipc and sentenced to undergo R.I. for
20 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- with default stipulation.

entities.text:
Protection of Children
from Sexual Offence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellant submits that the appellant remained in custody for about 1 and 1/2 years.
The final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.

Learned counsel for the appellant by taking this Court to the prosecution story it is submitted that written report was lodged by the prosecutrix on 09.05.2018 that she and appellant became friends and during that period, he mixed some substance in the tea which was consumed by the prosecutrix and she became unconscious.

During that period, appellant took certain objectionable photos of the victim and on the strength of those photos, he blackmailed her and committed sexual assault on number of times for a long period of time.
When he was fed up with the threatening and such assaults, she lodged the report.

Criticizing the prosecution story Shri Siddharth Datt learned counsel for appellant placed heavy reliance on the findings of trial court mentioned in paragraphs 38 and 57 of the judgment, it is argued that these findings in no uncertain terms make it clear that the appellant and victim were having cordial relation.

The story that appellant mixed something in the tea because of which victim got unconscious and taking advantage of that the appellant took her objectionable photographs was disbelieved by the trial court itself.
There is a specific finding that the appellant neither used and circulated those objectionable photographs nor threatened the victim by using those photographs.
It is submitted that the determination of age of victim by the Court below is bad in law, thus remaining jail sentence may be suspended.

sentences.text: Shri Ajay Shukla, learned Government Advocate opposed the prayer on the basis of objection.
Considering the aforesaid factual backdrop and without expressing any conclusive opinion on the merits of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of this appellant.

Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the remaining jail sentence of appellant is hereby suspended and it is directed that appellant Shubham Chouhan @ Kala be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with separate solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court, Bhopal on 11.03.2024 and also on such other dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this Appeal.
